48.original: You look like a ssstrider in sssearch of comrades in need. If ssso, I have a tasssk for you.

49.original: I am a trainer, and I was told to expect new recruitsss thisss <hex:02082DE3E90C0DFF1302080FE3E90C05FF04657665FF0464617903FF1302080FE3E90C12FF04646179FF046576650303>, yet nary a one has come. Perhapsss they were given the wrong time or location. I do not know.

50.original: They number five in all, these would-be warriors. Sssend them unto me, should you chance to find them.

51.original: With time, I can turn even the most haplesss milksssops into whirlwinds of death. But I cannot do thisss if sssaid farm boys do not come.

52.original: Oh bugger, you were sent by the snake, weren't you!? I heard one in four recruits doesn't live through their training. That can't be true, right? Oh bugger, oh bugger...

53.original: Ah. A thousand pardons. So preoccupied was I by the question of whether Ala Mhigo should be a monarchy or republic that I neglected to attend my training. How silly, I know─until we drive the imperials from our lands, the question is moot.

54.original: I know, I know. I'm late. But I had to say a prayer for my sister first. After what the imperials did to her, death was a mercy...

55.original: Huh? Training? Gah! I was so busy practicing to impress the others that I completely forgot! Thank you!

56.original: The teacher calls for me? I see. We were discussing strategies for disabling magitek armor, you see, and... Ah, yes, of course, there is no time. If you would excuse me.

57.original: All recruitsss are presssent and accounted for. My thanksss to you, ssstrider.

58.original: Not all appreciate the rigor with which I train my recruitsss. Sssome favor a gentler approach. As if the imperials will be ssso kind.

59.original: 'Tis a thanklesss job, to teach, sssome sssay. But I sssay their sssurvival is thanksss enough. Fare you well.
